newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsuzuka sees temporary economic setback in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Mitsuzuka sees temporary economic setback in 97/98.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday that he expects the Japanese economy to experience a temporary setback in the first half of this fiscal year but added that this would not undermine an economic recovery spearheaded by private-sector demand.

"I see a temporary (economic) setback in the first half of the current fiscal year, but that will not undermine the recovery led by private demand," Mitsuzuka said in a speech to journalists and business executives.

Mitsuzuka said efforts were being made to resolve bad-loan problems in the financial sector, and that such efforts would likely have a significant impact on the economy by improving the economic outlook of corporations and consumers.
Mitsuzuka said the disposal of bad loans by domestic financial institutions was progressing smoothly.
"I think financial institutions as a whole will be able to overcome it (the bad loan problem)," he said.

Mitsuzuka praised the recent announcement of a planned alliance between Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) and Bankers Trust New York Corp, and added that there may be more alliances between Japanese and foreign financial institutions in future.
"We hold a positive view about the alliance between NCB and Bankers Trust," he said.
Mitsuzuka also said Japan does not intend to use exports as a prime locomotive for growth.

"Japan will not use exports as the prime locomotive for growth. Instead, the country is carrying out balanced management of economic policies that puts emphasis on achieving sustainable growth led by private-sector demand," he said.
In the long run, this stance would benefit Japan's trading partners as well as Japan's economy, he said.
